# Running The Living Studio

**The Living Studio** is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation:
an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact
Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent
connected to the MCP server.

The Studio runs three ways locally, plus a hosted deployment. All of them serve
the same SPA, which talks only to the sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:8100` — the
SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM directly.

## Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────────┐  /api (JSON)  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
│  Living Studio SPA         │ ────────────▶ │  apps/studio-api (sidecar)    │
│  React + TS + Vite         │  /api/chat    │  FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100    │
│  (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │  - config / health / canvas   │
└────────────────────────────┘  SSE stream   │  - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │
                                             │  - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop)  │
                                             │  - conversations + PM memory  │
                                             └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                             │ MCP (HTTP)
                                                             ▼
                                             ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                             │  apps/mcp-server :8000/mcp    │
                                             └───────────────────────────────┘
                                                             ▲
                                                             │ OpenAI-compatible
                                             ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                                             │  Your local LLM backend       │
                                             └───────────────────────────────┘
```

## Interface

The Studio opens as a conversation, not a dashboard.

| Surface | What it does |
|---|---|
| **First-run tour** | A four-step, skippable welcome on the very first visit: what the studio is, which ambition brought you here, the live state of your sidecar/MCP/model (with inline repair when the model is down), and the first move. The four doors are **I have one in mind**, **My boss handed me a priority**, **Help me find the next one**, and **Pressure-test a bet**; each starts the matching conversation. Replay it from **Settings → Replay the welcome tour**. |
| **First run** | A short conversation in the chat, not a form: what you are building, who feels the problem, the job they are trying to get done, then where it hurts. One question at a time, with a reflection before the next ask, quick replies, and **Explore on my own** always visible. Skipping is allowed; answers and progress are kept as a draft. Re-open it any time with `/start`, the home stage's context pill, or Settings. |
| **Hero** | One rotating headline above the composer: a greeting (time of day, plus your name if you set one in Settings), the product/job you set up, what is already on the canvas, or an intent-first prompt such as *What are you trying to win this quarter?* It cycles every few seconds and stays still under `prefers-reduced-motion`. |
| **Suggestion pills** | Below the headline. **Sharpen an opportunity** always starts a conversation; the next pill becomes **Pressure-test a bet** once outcomes exist, or **Find the next opportunity** before that. **Capture what you heard** replaces the landscape pill once a job exists. They change as the canvas fills up. |
| **Composer** | Docked at the bottom of the transcript. `Enter` sends, `Shift`+`Enter` adds a line, `Cmd/Ctrl`+`K` focuses it, and `/` opens the command palette. The send button becomes a stop button while a reply streams. |
| **Bar** | The only persistent chrome: home, new conversation, catch-up, live model status, and settings. There is no navigation drawer to compete with the thread. |
| **Rail** | Above the conversation, and only once the thread has produced something: `Landscape · N`, `Job map · N`, `Evidence · N`, `What I know · N`. Every item is derived from the canvas and the memory, so the strip is a record of the work rather than a fixed menu. |
| **Lens** | A view docks to the right of the thread on wide screens and becomes a full-height sheet on narrow ones. The transcript and the composer stay on screen and stay usable; `Esc`, **Close**, or the rail chip closes it. Every lens ends in one sentence that re-enters the conversation — *Ask which to chase*, *Walk me through the job*, *Weigh the evidence* — so leaving a view is never a return to a menu. Settings and catch-up use the same lens. |

Replies render Markdown (headings, lists, emphasis, inline and fenced code).
Tool calls appear inline as small trace chips while the agent works.

### Slash commands

Type `/` to open the palette. `Up`/`Down` move, `Enter` or `Tab` runs the
selected command, `Esc` closes it. Commands are handled in the SPA and never call
the model, so they work when it is offline.

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/help` | Every command, as a notice in the transcript |
| `/start` | Resume the context conversation |
| `/new` | New conversation |
| `/home` | Return to the empty stage |
| `/jobs` | Job summary, then the job map |
| `/landscape`, `/jobmap`, `/evidence`, `/settings` | Open that lens beside the conversation |
| `/impact`, `/capture` | Start the conversation that produces the card. `/capture` falls back to the offline form when no model answers. |
| `/status` | Model, MCP, context, and canvas status |

Unknown commands produce a transcript notice pointing at `/help`.

### The welcome tour

The tour is the front door, the context conversation is the first room. It is
skippable at every step (`Skip the tour` or `Escape`), resumable (progress is
stored after every transition in `localStorage["studio.onboarding"]`), and
replayable from Settings.

Everything lives in `apps/studio/src/onboarding/`:

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `content.ts` | Steps and goal copy as typed data — the only place the words live |
| `machine.ts` | Pure state transitions, no React or storage |
| `storage.ts` | Versioned, defensive `localStorage` persistence |
| `OnboardingProvider.tsx` | Auto-open, persistence, replay |
| `FirstRunWizard.tsx`, `steps.tsx`, `onboarding.css` | The dialog |
| `../features/flags.ts` | The `firstRunWizard` toggle |

`App.tsx` only wires the provider and the wizard around the existing shell;
the chat, canvas, and sidecar code are untouched.

#### Toggling the tour

`firstRunWizard` defaults to on. Resolution order, highest first:

| Source | Example | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Query parameter | `?flags=firstRunWizard:off` | QA a build without rebuilding |
| Local override | `localStorage["studio.flags.firstRunWizard"] = "off"` | Per-browser opt-out |
| Build environment | `VITE_STUDIO_FIRST_RUN_WIZARD=off npm --prefix apps/studio run build` | Ship it dark |
| Default | on | |

Accepted values are `1`/`0`, `true`/`false`, `on`/`off`, `yes`/`no`, and
`enabled`/`disabled`. With the flag off, no dialog renders, no onboarding state
is written, and Settings hides the replay action.

### Guidance, not gates

The setup conversation is a nudge, never a prerequisite. If you skip it, the
home stage keeps a dashed **Tell me what you're building** pill; it reopens the
conversation exactly where you left off. `/start` and Settings do the same. The conversation also understands a
natural reply: say "skip", "not now", or "show me the landscape" and it reacts
instead of recording it as an answer. When a brief exists, it opens on a review
and asks what changed rather than asking everything again.

### Without a model

When the LLM is unreachable the Studio keeps working:

- A **Working by hand** strip explains the state and offers capture, job map,
  and context.
- Messages still return deterministic ODI guidance from the sidecar, labelled
  **Local guidance**.
- Jobs can be created, renamed, and deleted; steps added, edited, and removed;
  outcomes recorded, re-scored, and removed. All of it goes through the same
  local repository the model uses.
- Settings → Base URL and Model reconnect the assistant whenever you are ready.

The user's context is sent with every chat request, so the assistant starts from
the product, audience, job, and problem rather than asking for them again.

### The thread is the room

Capture, scoring, simulation, and decisions are conversations. The storefront
never asks the PM to leave the thread to do work: the agent asks for the
customer's words or the bet in plain language, then renders the surface that
carries it. A lens exists for reading and for people who prefer a click, not for
doing the work.

That is also enforced in the agent's system prompt: it is told to keep every
artifact in the conversation, never to send the PM to a panel, and to end each
reply with the next move as an action on the surface.

### What it remembers

The studio keeps a small, local, editable model of the person it is helping. It
is not a profile and not a transcript index; it is the handful of things that
change the next answer.

| Kind | What it captures |
|---|---|
| `career` | The PM's role, remit, and what success looks like for them |
| `opportunity` | The opportunity or bet currently in play |
| `business` | Goals, metrics, and commercial constraints |
| `stakeholder` | Who else matters and what they care about |
| `constraint` | Time, budget, policy, or technical limits |
| `evidence` | What has actually been heard or measured |
| `preference` | How the PM likes to work and be spoken to |

Each note is `suggested` or `confirmed`. Suggested notes appear first under
**What I know** with **Yes, that's right**, **That's not it**, and **Edit**;
confirmed notes can be edited or forgotten. The PM can also add a note by hand.
Nothing is silently promoted: the agent may propose, but the person decides.

The agent writes notes through a `remember` tool during a normal reply. The
sidecar applies it, emits a `memory` SSE event, and the panel updates without a
refresh. Memory writes are best-effort — a database failure never turns a good
answer into an error.

Storage is a separate SQLite file from the ODI repository:
`~/.agentic-odi/studio.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`
(`:memory:` is supported and is what the tests use). The API is small:

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/memory/observations` | Everything the agent believes |
| `POST` | `/api/memory/observations` | Add a note by hand |
| `PATCH` | `/api/memory/observations/{id}` | Edit text, confidence, or status |
| `DELETE` | `/api/memory/observations/{id}` | Forget one note |
| `DELETE` | `/api/memory` | Forget all notes and conversations |

**Forget everything** is a two-step confirmation and also clears the visible
thread, because the server deletes the conversations behind it.

### The thread comes back

Conversations are stored beside the memory. On launch the SPA asks
`GET /api/conversations/latest`, restores that thread's user and assistant
turns, and continues with the same `conversation_id` on the next message. **New
conversation** starts a fresh one without touching the memory; **Forget
everything** removes both. The composer stays usable while the restore is in
flight, and a restore failure simply leaves the room empty.

## Rich responses

The copilot does not only talk. When a surface carries the evidence better than a
paragraph, the agent renders one **inline in the conversation**: a scored
outcome, a ranked opportunity board, a before/after simulation of a bet, a
customer quote with its lineage, the eight-stage job map, an opportunity thesis, or a decision record.
Three properties keep this safe and cheap to extend:

- **The catalog is closed and owned by the SPA.**
  `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` declares nine primitives and seven cards, their
  JSON Schema props, and the description the model reads. There is no HTML, no
  eval, and no third-party component in the path. Prose is rendered by the same
  `Markdown` component the transcript already used.
- **The sidecar is catalog-agnostic.** The SPA sends the catalog with each turn;
  the sidecar derives the `render_ui` tool schema from it, validates what comes
  back, and streams a `ui` SSE event. Invalid props return to the model as a tool
  result naming the exact violation, and the loop offers the tool again, so a
  fumbled prop is corrected in the same reply. A client that sends no catalog
  never sees the tool.
- **Cards are views, never actors.** Every button is an `intent` string that the
  agent receives as the user's next message — one authority, one audit trail.

A surface is one node tree, streamed as one event:

```json
{
  "type": "outcome-card",
  "props": {
    "id": "O-1",
    "statement": "Minimize the time it takes to propagate secrets across environments",
    "importance": 9,
    "satisfaction": 3
  }
}
```

The opportunity thesis is the intent-first card: one opportunity with its
importance, satisfaction, the gap in plain words, the thesis itself, and the
smallest next move. It is the shape the agent reaches for when the PM is deciding
what to chase, rather than when they are inspecting a single score.

The conversation keeps the order the agent produced: a `delta` appends to the
open prose part, a `ui` event opens a card, and the next `delta` opens a new
paragraph after it. The opportunity score is computed from importance and
satisfaction when the agent omits it, so the ODI formula has exactly one home
(`src/lib/odi.ts`). Unknown component types degrade to a quiet fallback; a tree
that fails validation is dropped whole, and the surrounding prose still reads.

### Adding a surface

1. Add an entry to `CATALOG` in `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` — props as a
   JSON Schema subset, plus the description the model will read.
2. Register the component in `apps/studio/src/ui/registry.ts`.
3. Implement it in `apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx` (domain shape) or
   `apps/studio/src/ui/primitives.tsx` (composition).
4. Run `npm --prefix apps/studio test`. The `registry parity` test fails if the
   catalog and the registry drift apart.

No server change is needed, and no new dependency.

## Hosted (experimental)

The built SPA is also served from Cloudflare Workers at
**[https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**.
The UI loads without a backend; canvas data, chat, and mutations need the local
sidecar and MCP server. Pull requests get preview URLs from Cloudflare Workers
Builds. See [Deployment](deployment.md) for the Worker setup.

## 1. Web — production build (recommended for a quick look)

```bash
npm --prefix apps/studio run build   # build the SPA into apps/studio/dist
python scripts/dev.py            # starts MCP :8000 + sidecar :8100
```

| Service | URL |
|---|---|
| MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp |
| Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 |

`python scripts/dev.py` starts both processes concurrently; press **Ctrl+C** to
stop both.

## 2. Web — dev with hot reload

Vite proxies `/api` to the sidecar:

```bash
npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full   # MCP + sidecar + Vite together
# open http://localhost:5173
```

## 3. Desktop — Tauri 2

The app spawns the MCP server and sidecar itself:

```bash
npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev     # dev window
npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri build   # bundles: .deb / .AppImage (Linux), .app / .dmg (macOS), .msi / .exe (Windows)
```

> [!NOTE]
> **Tauri prerequisites.** The desktop build needs the WebKitGTK toolchain and
> Rust 1.90+. On Debian/Ubuntu:
>
> ```bash
> sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential pkg-config curl wget file \
>   libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf xdg-utils libfuse2t64
> ```
>
> The Tauri CLI ships as the `@tauri-apps/cli` npm dev dependency
> (`npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri`). The sidecar is launched with
> `uv run python -m …` from the repository root; if the app cannot locate the
> repo root, set `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT`.

## Desktop signing & updater secrets

Self-updating and code signing are **env-driven**: if a secret is absent, an
unsigned artifact is produced instead of failing. CI reads these from GitHub
Actions secrets.

| Secret | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | Signs updater artifacts (`.sig`) and the `latest.json` manifest. A tagged release fails loudly without it. Generate with `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate`. |
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | Password for the private key (optional when the key has none). |
| `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` / `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | macOS Developer ID certificate (base64 `.p12`) and its password. |
| `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` | macOS signing identity. |
| `APPLE_ID` / `APPLE_PASSWORD` / `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | macOS notarization credentials. |
| `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE` / `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | Windows Authenticode PFX (base64) and its password; imported by CI and injected into the bundle config. |

Releases are published by `.github/workflows/tauri-release.yml` when a `v*` tag
is pushed. The desktop app checks for updates on startup and via
**Settings → Check for updates**.

### Managing the updater signing key

The updater key pair authenticates release artifacts so an installed app can
verify that an auto-update genuinely came from you. The **public** key is
embedded in `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (`plugins.updater.pubkey`) and is
safe to commit. The **private** key must never be committed, logged, printed in
CI, or attached to a build artifact.

1. **Generate a key pair** (only if you need a new one). Leave `-p ""` for a
   passwordless key, or pass a password and remember it:

   ```bash
   npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate -- -w ./living-studio.key -p "" -f
   ```

   This writes `living-studio.key` (private, `0600`) and `living-studio.key.pub`
   (public).

2. **Paste the public key** into `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`:

   ```jsonc
   {
     "plugins": {
       "updater": {
         "endpoints": ["https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/latest.json"],
         "pubkey": "<contents of living-studio.key.pub>"
       }
     }
   }
   ```

3. **Store the private key outside the repository** (the repo root is
   git-tracked; a sibling directory is not), with restricted permissions:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys && chmod 700 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys
   mv living-studio.key ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/
   chmod 600 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
   ```

   Move it to a long-term secret store (password manager, 1Password/Bitwarden/
   Vault, or a private encrypted backup) when you decide where that lives.
   Losing it means future releases can no longer be signed for existing
   installs.

4. **Add the private key as a GitHub Actions secret** (Settings → Secrets and
   variables → Actions → New repository secret), or via the CLI:

   ```bash
   gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
   gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD --body ""   # only if you set a password
   ```

5. **Verify** the secrets exist (values are never displayed):

   ```bash
   gh secret list
   ```

6. **Rotate** by repeating steps 1–4, then publishing a release signed with the
   new key. Existing installs still verify against the public key compiled into
   their binary, so keep the old private key usable and publish the new public
   key ahead of the cut-over.

> [!CAUTION]
> If the private key leaks, treat auto-updates as compromised: generate a new
> pair, rotate the Actions secret, and publish a freshly signed release.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Migration note.** The Streamlit UI has been removed. The Living Studio now
> lives in `apps/studio/` (browser SPA + Tauri desktop app) and is served by the
> `apps/studio-api` sidecar on port **8100** (previously Streamlit's `8501`).
> Start everything with `python scripts/dev.py`. All `AGENTIC_ODI_*` environment
> variable names, the demo dataset, and the ODI formulas are unchanged.

## Connecting an LLM

The Studio needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM backend with tool-calling support to
drive the agent. For a fully local setup, see
[Local LLM Backend](local-llm.md).

## Agent-Driven Testing

Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it starts
both processes, opens the browser, sends a test message, and reports the results.

Type `/test` to have the agent run all tests and report the results
automatically.

1: """Self-update engine primitives (checksum, extraction, atomic version swap)."""
2: 
3: from __future__ import annotations
4: 
5: import hashlib
6: import json
7: import os
8: import platform
9: import shutil
10: import tarfile
11: import tempfile
12: import urllib.request
13: import zipfile
14: from collections.abc import Callable
15: from pathlib import Path
16: from urllib.parse import urlparse
17: 
18: from agentic_odi_cli import paths
19: from agentic_odi_cli.version import __version__
20: 
21: RELEASES_API = "https://api.github.com/repos/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest"
22: CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 86400
23: _RELEASES_DOWNLOAD = "https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/download"
24: 
25: _SYSTEM_MAP = {"Linux": "linux", "Darwin": "macos", "Windows": "windows"}
26: _ARCH_MAP = {
27:     "x86_64": "x86_64",
28:     "AMD64": "x86_64",
29:     "arm64": "arm64",
30:     "aarch64": "arm64",
31: }
32: 
33: 
34: class UpdateError(Exception):
35:     """Raised when an update cannot be performed."""
36: 
37: 
38: def parse_version(s: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
39:     """Parse a version string into a ``(major, minor, patch)`` tuple."""
40:     cleaned = s.strip().lstrip("v")
41:     parts = cleaned.split(".")[:3]
42:     nums = [int(p) for p in parts]
43:     while len(nums) < 3:
44:         nums.append(0)
45:     return (nums[0], nums[1], nums[2])
46: 
47: 
48: def is_newer(latest: str, current: str) -> bool:
49:     """Return True if ``latest`` is strictly newer than ``current``."""
50:     return parse_version(latest) > parse_version(current)
51: 
52: 
53: def asset_name(version: str, os_name: str, arch: str) -> str:
54:     """Return the release asset filename for a version/platform combination."""
55:     ext = "zip" if os_name == "windows" else "tar.gz"
56:     return f"odi_{version}_{os_name}_{arch}.{ext}"
57: 
58: 
59: def current_platform() -> tuple[str, str]:
60:     """Map the running host to the release ``(os, arch)`` identifiers."""
61:     os_name = _SYSTEM_MAP.get(platform.system(), platform.system().lower())
62:     arch = _ARCH_MAP.get(platform.machine(), platform.machine().lower())
63:     return os_name, arch
64: 
65: 
66: def verify_checksum(path: Path, expected_hex: str) -> bool:
67:     """Return True if the SHA-256 of ``path`` matches ``expected_hex``."""
68:     digest = hashlib.sha256()
69:     with path.open("rb") as handle:
70:         for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(65536), b""):
71:             digest.update(chunk)
72:     return digest.hexdigest().lower() == expected_hex.strip().lower()
73: 
74: 
75: def extract_archive(archive: Path, dest: Path) -> None:
76:     """Extract ``archive`` (``.zip`` or ``.tar.gz``) into ``dest``."""
77:     dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
78:     if archive.name.endswith(".zip"):
79:         with zipfile.ZipFile(archive) as zf:
80:             zf.extractall(dest)  # nosec B202 - ZipFile strips absolute/'..' member paths
81:     else:
82:         with tarfile.open(archive, "r:gz") as tf:
83:             tf.extractall(dest, filter="data")
84: 
85: 
86: def _acquire_lock(install_root: Path) -> tuple[int, Path]:
87:     lock_path = install_root / ".update.lock"
88:     try:
89:         fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY)
90:     except FileExistsError as exc:
91:         raise UpdateError("update already in progress") from exc
92:     return fd, lock_path
93: 
94: 
95: def _activate_version(version_dir: Path, install_root: Path) -> None:
96:     current = install_root / "current"
97:     if os.name == "nt":
98:         marker_tmp = install_root / "current.tmp"
99:         if marker_tmp.exists() or marker_tmp.is_symlink():
100:             marker_tmp.unlink()
101:         marker_tmp.write_text(str(version_dir))
102:         os.replace(marker_tmp, current)
103:         return
104: 
105:     tmp_link = install_root / "current.tmp"
106:     if tmp_link.is_symlink() or tmp_link.exists():
107:         tmp_link.unlink()
108:     os.symlink(version_dir, tmp_link)
109:     os.replace(tmp_link, current)
110: 
111: 
112: def perform_update(
113:     version: str,
114:     archive_path: Path,
115:     expected_sha: str,
116:     install_root: Path,
117: ) -> Path:
118:     """Verify, extract, and atomically activate ``version``; return its dir."""
119:     install_root = Path(install_root)
120:     versions = install_root / "versions"
121:     versions.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
122: 
123:     lock_fd, lock_path = _acquire_lock(install_root)
124:     try:
125:         if not verify_checksum(archive_path, expected_sha):
126:             raise UpdateError(f"checksum mismatch for {archive_path.name}")
127: 
128:         tmp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=".extract-", dir=versions))
129:         final_dir = versions / version
130:         try:
131:             extract_archive(archive_path, tmp_dir)
132:             if final_dir.is_symlink() or final_dir.is_file():
133:                 final_dir.unlink()
134:             elif final_dir.is_dir():
135:                 shutil.rmtree(final_dir)
136:             os.replace(tmp_dir, final_dir)
137:         except BaseException:
138:             shutil.rmtree(tmp_dir, ignore_errors=True)
139:             raise
140: 
141:         _activate_version(final_dir, install_root)
142:         return final_dir
143:     finally:
144:         os.close(lock_fd)
145:         try:
146:             lock_path.unlink()
147:         except FileNotFoundError:
148:             pass
149: 
150: 
151: def should_check(state_file: Path, now: float) -> bool:
152:     """Return True if an update check is due (missing/corrupt state ⇒ due)."""
153:     try:
154:         data = json.loads(Path(state_file).read_text())
155:         last_check = float(data["last_check"])
156:     except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
157:         return True
158:     return (now - last_check) >= CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS
159: 
160: 
161: def record_check(state_file: Path, now: float) -> None:
162:     """Persist the timestamp of the most recent check."""
163:     path = Path(state_file)
164:     path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
165:     path.write_text(json.dumps({"last_check": now}))
166: 
167: 
168: def _require_https(url: str) -> None:
169:     """Reject anything that is not plain HTTPS before it can be opened."""
170:     if urlparse(url).scheme != "https":
171:         raise UpdateError(f"refusing non-HTTPS URL: {url}")
172: 
173: 
174: def _default_fetch(url: str) -> str:
175:     _require_https(url)
176:     with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=10) as response:  # nosec B310 - _require_https
177:         return response.read().decode("utf-8")
178: 
179: 
180: def _default_fetch_bytes(url: str) -> bytes:
181:     _require_https(url)
182:     with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=10) as response:  # nosec B310 - _require_https
183:         return response.read()
184: 
185: 
186: def latest_release(current: str, *, fetch: Callable[[str], str] | None = None) -> str | None:
187:     """Return the latest release version if newer than ``current``, else None."""
188:     fetcher = fetch if fetch is not None else _default_fetch
189:     try:
190:         payload = json.loads(fetcher(RELEASES_API))
191:         tag = str(payload["tag_name"]).strip()
192:     except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
193:         return None
194:     latest = tag.lstrip("v")
195:     if is_newer(latest, current):
196:         return latest
197:     return None
198: 
199: 
200: def _parse_checksums(text: str, filename: str) -> str | None:
201:     """Return the SHA-256 hex for ``filename`` from a sha256sum-format body."""
202:     for line in text.splitlines():
203:         parts = line.split()
204:         if len(parts) >= 2 and parts[1] == filename:
205:             return parts[0]
206:     return None
207: 
208: 
209: def download(
210:     version: str,
211:     dest_dir: Path,
212:     *,
213:     fetch_bytes: Callable[[str], bytes] | None = None,
214: ) -> Path:
215:     """Download and verify the release archive for ``version``."""
216:     fetcher = fetch_bytes if fetch_bytes is not None else _default_fetch_bytes
217:     base = f"{_RELEASES_DOWNLOAD}/v{version}"
218:     asset = asset_name(version, *current_platform())
219: 
220:     try:
221:         checksums = fetcher(f"{base}/checksums.txt").decode("utf-8")
222:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
223:         raise UpdateError(f"failed to fetch checksums.txt: {exc}") from exc
224: 
225:     expected = _parse_checksums(checksums, asset)
226:     if expected is None:
227:         raise UpdateError(f"no checksum entry for {asset}")
228: 
229:     try:
230:         payload = fetcher(f"{base}/{asset}")
231:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
232:         raise UpdateError(f"failed to fetch {asset}: {exc}") from exc
233: 
234:     dest_dir = Path(dest_dir)
235:     dest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
236:     dest = dest_dir / asset
237:     dest.write_bytes(payload)
238:     if not verify_checksum(dest, expected):
239:         raise UpdateError(f"checksum mismatch for {asset}")
240:     return dest
241: 
242: 
243: def auto_update_enabled(no_update: bool) -> bool:
244:     """Return whether auto-update is enabled by the flag/env opt-outs."""
245:     return (not no_update) and (not os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE"))
246: 
247: 
248: def maybe_auto_update(*, no_update: bool, now: float) -> str | None:
249:     """Best-effort background update; never raises, returns new version or None."""
250:     try:
251:         if not auto_update_enabled(no_update):
252:             return None
253:         root = paths.install_root()
254:         if not paths.is_frozen():
255:             return None
256:         if not paths.is_writable_dir(root):
257:             return None
258:         if (root / ".update.lock").exists():
259:             return None
260:         state = paths.state_file()
261:         if not should_check(state, now):
262:             return None
263:         record_check(state, now)
264:         version = latest_release(__version__)
265:         if version is None:
266:             return None
267:         with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="odi-update-") as tmp:
268:             archive = download(version, Path(tmp))
269:             digest = hashlib.sha256(archive.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
270:             perform_update(version, archive, digest, root)
271:         return version
272:     except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
273:         return None

1: # Odi the Otter — brand guide
2: 
3: Odi is the mascot of **Agentic ODI**: a golden-ratio-derived pixel otter who
4: appears in the CLI, the Living Studio, the desktop app icon, the favicon, and
5: the README.
6: 
7: He is an otter because otters are the tool-using problem solvers of the animal
8: world — they take an ambiguous shell, a stone, and a current and *engineer* an
9: outcome from it. That is the product in one animal: turn messy human context
10: into a measurable customer outcome. No widely known developer tool uses an
11: otter, so the silhouette is unclaimed, and no other mascot in the category is
12: a feline, a penguin, a gopher, or an octopus.
13: 
14: **Odi is original work**, built from geometric primitives by the committed
15: generator in `brand/src/odi_mascot.py`, and covered by the repository's MIT
16: `LICENSE`. A mascot is a weak trademark; what this buys is *provenance* — a
17: fork that ships Odi has visibly forked Agentic ODI.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## Palette
22: 
23: | Token | Hex | Use |
24: |---|---|---|
25: | `odi-ink` | `#1B1410` | outline, nose, pupils |
26: | `odi-fur` | `#B4794C` | main coat |
27: | `odi-fur-light` | `#DCA871` | cheeks |
28: | `odi-cream` | `#F6EAD8` | muzzle, chest, eye highlight |
29: | `odi-accent` | `#8B8CF8` | the spark — the studio's existing accent |
30: | `odi-tile` | `#131722` | app-icon tile — matches the site mark tile |
31: 
32: The only new colours in the system are the coat browns. Everything else was
33: already in the product: `#8B8CF8` is the studio accent and `#131722` is the
34: tile the site mark sits on.
35: 
36: ### Measured contrast
37: 
38: Every ratio below is measured, not asserted, and is pinned by
39: `brand/tests/test_brand_assets.py`.
40: 
41: | Pairing | Ratio | Reading |
42: |---|---|---|
43: | `odi-ink` on `odi-fur` | 5.01:1 | the outline that defines the face — passes AA for text |
44: | `odi-ink` on `odi-cream` | 15.32:1 | the nose and mouth on the muzzle |
45: | `odi-fur` on `odi-cream` | 3.06:1 | the coat against the muzzle — a non-text boundary, passes 3:1 |
46: | `odi-fur` on studio `#0a0b0e` | 5.42:1 | Odi on the app's near-black chrome |
47: | `odi-fur` on `odi-tile` | 4.93:1 | Odi on the app-icon tile |
48: | `odi-accent` on studio `#0a0b0e` | 6.75:1 | the spark |
49: | `odi-accent` on `odi-tile` | 6.14:1 | the spark on the tile |
50: | `odi-cream` on `odi-tile` | 15.07:1 | the muzzle on the tile |
51: 
52: `odi-ink` on the near-black chrome is 1.08:1 by design: the outline is never
53: meant to be read against the background, only against the fur it encloses.
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## The golden-ratio construction
58: 
59: Every proportion of Odi's head comes from one constant, φ = 1.6180339887,
60: applied to the head width **W** (20 px in the bust, 22 px in the icon). The
61: head's internal proportions are scale-invariant, so the icon renders the same
62: animal at a different size.

display.text:
# Odi the Otter — brand guide

Odi is the mascot of **Agentic ODI**: a golden-ratio-derived pixel otter who
appears in the CLI, the Living Studio, the desktop app icon, the favicon, and
the README.

He is an otter because otters are the tool-using problem solvers of the animal
world — they take an ambiguous shell, a stone, and a current and *engineer* an
outcome from it. That is the product in one animal: turn messy human context
into a measurable customer outcome. No widely known developer tool uses an
otter, so the silhouette is unclaimed, and no other mascot in the category is
a feline, a penguin, a gopher, or an octopus.

**Odi is original work**, built from geometric primitives by the committed
generator in `brand/src/odi_mascot.py`, and covered by the repository's MIT
`LICENSE`. A mascot is a weak trademark; what this buys is *provenance* — a
fork that ships Odi has visibly forked Agentic ODI.

---

## Palette

| Token | Hex | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `odi-ink` | `#1B1410` | outline, nose, pupils |
| `odi-fur` | `#B4794C` | main coat |
| `odi-fur-light` | `#DCA871` | cheeks |
| `odi-cream` | `#F6EAD8` | muzzle, chest, eye highlight |
| `odi-accent` | `#8B8CF8` | the spark — the studio's existing accent |
| `odi-tile` | `#131722` | app-icon tile — matches the site mark tile |

The only new colours in the system are the coat browns. Everything else was
already in the product: `#8B8CF8` is the studio accent and `#131722` is the
tile the site mark sits on.

### Measured contrast

Every ratio below is measured, not asserted, and is pinned by
`brand/tests/test_brand_assets.py`.

| Pairing | Ratio | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| `odi-ink` on `odi-fur` | 5.01:1 | the outline that defines the face — passes AA for text |
| `odi-ink` on `odi-cream` | 15.32:1 | the nose and mouth on the muzzle |
| `odi-fur` on `odi-cream` | 3.06:1 | the coat against the muzzle — a non-text boundary, passes 3:1 |
| `odi-fur` on studio `#0a0b0e` | 5.42:1 | Odi on the app's near-black chrome |
| `odi-fur` on `odi-tile` | 4.93:1 | Odi on the app-icon tile |
| `odi-accent` on studio `#0a0b0e` | 6.75:1 | the spark |
| `odi-accent` on `odi-tile` | 6.14:1 | the spark on the tile |
| `odi-cream` on `odi-tile` | 15.07:1 | the muzzle on the tile |

`odi-ink` on the near-black chrome is 1.08:1 by design: the outline is never
meant to be read against the background, only against the fur it encloses.

---

## The golden-ratio construction

Every proportion of Odi's head comes from one constant, φ = 1.6180339887,
applied to the head width **W** (20 px in the bust, 22 px in the icon). The
head's internal proportions are scale-invariant, so the icon renders the same
animal at a different size.

| Feature | Rule | Value (px) |
|---|---|---|
| Canvas | — | 32 × 32 |
| Head width `W` | unit | 20 (bust) / 22 (icon) |
| Head height | `W / φ` | 12 |
| Eye separation | `W / φ` | 12 |
| Eye size | `W / φ²`, capped | 4 × 4 |
| Muzzle width | `W / φ²` | 8 |
| Muzzle height | `(W / φ²) / φ` | 5 |
| Nose width | `W / φ³` | 5 |
| Ear radius | `W / 4φ` | 3 |
| Body width | `0.85 × W` | 17 |

**The head is a golden rectangle** — 20 wide by 12 tall is 1.667, within 3% of
φ once the height is rounded to a whole pixel. **The face divides at the
golden section**: the eyes sit 0.618 of the head width apart, the muzzle is
0.382 of it, and the nose is 0.236 of it. **The body is 0.85 of the head** —
the chibi proportion, which is the same golden rule applied to mass, where
the smaller partner of a golden pair reads as "just right".

`brand/assets/odi-mascot.svg` carries the construction as a visible
`data-guides="true"` layer: the head rectangle, the eye-separation line, and
the muzzle box. Open it in a browser or an editor to see the grid the art was
drawn on.

---

## The three variants

| Variant | Contents | Where it is used |
|---|---|---|
| `head` | skull, ears, eyes, muzzle, nose, mouth | the base for the other two |
| `mark` | the head on the `odi-tile` rounded square | app icon, favicon, studio brand mark |
| `bust` | head, shoulders, chest, and the spark | README hero, brand guide |

The `mark` exists because operating-system icons want a filled shape (Windows
`StoreLogo`, macOS `.icns`) while a browser tab and a toolbar want the
character standing on its own. Both share the identical head.

---

## Files

```text
brand/
  assets/        the committed artwork (generated)
  src/           the generator — the single source of truth
  tests/         the asset contract and the drift check
  tools/render.py  regenerates everything
```

Regenerate every Odi artifact — the PNGs, the SVGs, the ICO, the studio
component, and the CLI banner — with one command:

```bash
uv run python brand/tools/render.py
```

Check that nothing has drifted:

```bash
uv run python brand/tools/render.py --check
```

CI runs that check, so the committed artwork can never silently disagree with
the code that made it.

---

## Usage rules

- **Never scale the art to a non-integer size.** The master grid is 32 × 32.
  Render it at 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, or 1024 — a 28-pixel slot would
  scale the grid by 0.875 and blur it.
- **Never recolour `odi-ink`.** The outline is the character's structure.
- **Never place the head on a background other than `odi-tile`** in the `mark`
  variant. The bust is transparent and may sit on any dark surface.
- **Keep clear space of one head width** around the mark.
- **The mascot is decoration.** It is never the only label of a control, and
  it is always `aria-hidden` where it appears in the UI.
- **The spark is the signal.** It is the one element that carries the product's
  rising-outcome idea; do not remove it from the bust.

def test_content_is_visible_without_javascript():
    """Reveal-on-scroll must opt *in*, never opt out.

    The hidden state is scoped to `.js-reveal`, a class only the script adds.
    Without JavaScript nothing is hidden.
    """
    css = _css()
    hidden = re.search(r"\.js-reveal \[data-reveal\]\s*\{([^}]*)\}", css)
    assert hidden is not None, "the reveal rule is missing"
    assert "opacity: 0" in hidden.group(1)
    # The hidden state must not apply to a bare [data-reveal].
    assert not re.search(r"(?<!js-reveal )\n\[data-reveal\]\s*\{", css)

def test_the_layout_is_mobile_first_and_fluid():
    css = _css()
    assert "--w-page" not in css or True  # widths live in tokens.css
    assert "clamp(20px, 5vw, 48px)" in _tokens_css()  # gutter
    assert "max-width: 640px" in css
    assert "min-width: 760px" in css or "min-width: 960px" in css


def test_content_is_visible_without_javascript():
    """Reveal-on-scroll must opt *in*, never opt out.

    The hidden state is scoped to `.js-reveal`, a class only the script adds.
    Without JavaScript nothing is hidden.
    """
    css = _css()
    hidden = re.search(r"\.js-reveal \[data-reveal\]\s*\{([^}]*)\}", css)
    assert hidden is not None, "the reveal rule is missing"
    assert "opacity: 0" in hidden.group(1)
    # The hidden state must not apply to a bare [data-reveal].
    assert not re.search(r"(?<!js-reveal )\n\[data-reveal\]\s*\{", css)


def _tokens_css() -> str:
    return (SITE / "dist" / "assets" / "tokens.css").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

 * The closed catalog of surfaces the agent may compose.
 *
 * Two tiers, deliberately small: primitives for composition, cards for the ODI
 * shapes worth naming. Cards are leaves on the wire but render internally with
 * the same primitives, so the agent expresses intent ("score this outcome")
 * rather than layout.

 * to the sidecar; `catalogPrompt()` is what the model reads.
 */

parts.text:
So the catalog.ts has:
- Primitives section (lines 73-166): entries at lines 73, 84, 95, 106, 117, 128, 141, 154, 166 — that's 9 primitives
- A `divider` entry at line 166 (which is a primitive too, `entry("divider", "leaf", ...)`)
- Cards section (starting at line 168): entries at lines 169, 190, 214, 256, 268, 302, 318 — that's 7 cards

So the docs/living-studio.md claim of "nine primitives and seven cards" is correct!

Now, the `_cards.html` template comment says "The seven ODI cards the agent may compose" — correct.

And the landing.json says "Seven shapes" — correct.

OK so that's fine. Let me now focus on compiling my list of 12 concrete, high-value opportunities.

Let me also quickly check if there's anything in the `docs/architecture/README.md` about the wrangler.jsonc location being wrong.

Let me also check if the README's "Code Overview" table is accurate. It says:
- `infra/cloudflare/ | Worker | Free-plan Workers Static Assets deployment and sidecar tunnel.`

But the wrangler.jsonc is at the root, not in infra/cloudflare/. Only worker.ts is in infra/cloudflare/. So the README implies the wrangler config is in infra/cloudflare/ but it's actually at the root. This is a doc inaccuracy.

Now let me compile my 12 concrete opportunities. I'll focus on the most impactful, self-contained ones:

1. **Fix the `_mcp_reference.html` template: `odi_schema` should be `get_odi_schema`** — The MCP tool reference page displays `odi_schema` as the tool name in the heading, but the actual tool name is `get_odi_schema` (as correctly stated later in the same template on line 57). The `id="odi-schema"` is also inconsistent with the `id="tool-{name}"` pattern used for other tools. This is a self-contained fix in one template file.

2. **Remove or regenerate the stale `website/index.html`** — The root-level `website/index.html` is a hand-maintained file that's out of sync with the generated `website/dist/index.html` (which is the canonical output). It doesn't include the npm build step in the run section, has different title/description, and is not tested by any CI. It should either be removed (since the generated dist/ is the source of truth) or regenerated via the build system.

3. **Fix mypy command drift in `docs/development.md` and `docs/architecture/testing.md`** — Both docs list the wrong mypy invocation. `docs/development.md:17` says `uv run mypy apps packages` (missing `brand`), and `docs/architecture/testing.md:9` says `uv run mypy apps packages tests` (wrong: has `tests`, missing `brand`). CI ci.yml:46 runs `uv run mypy apps brand packages`.

4. **Fix bandit command drift in `docs/architecture/testing.md`** — Line 12 says `uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages` but CI also runs bandit on website: ci.yml:62 `uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r website/`.

5. **Document/fix the dual connectors config path/env var** — The CLI uses `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE` with default `Path.cwd() / ".agentic-odi" / "connectors.json"`, while the connectors package uses `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG` with default `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json`. The README mentions `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG` and `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json`, while docs/connectors.md mentions `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE` and `.agentic-odi/connectors.json`. The docs are inconsistent and don't explain why there are two different paths. This could confuse users.

6. **Fix the version mismatch between pyproject.toml and release-please manifest** — `pyproject.toml:3` says `version = "0.1.0"` but `.release-please-manifest.json` says `"0.12.0"`. This mismatch means the CLI would report version 0.1.0 while release-please proposes 0.12.0, causing confusion in the release flow.

7. **Remove the stale Streamlit migration note in `docs/living-studio.md`** — Lines 398-402 contain a migration note about Streamlit being removed, which is already complete. This note is outdated and should be removed or converted to historical context.

8. **Add a test for the `_mcp_reference.html` `odi_schema` → `get_odi_schema` fix** — After fixing #1, add an assertion in `test_content_sync.py` that the schema section references the correct tool name.

Actually, this should be bundled with #1. Let me think of separate opportunities.

9. **Add the CLI tree to the generated site docs** — The README claims "the CLI tree ... [is] read from the code that ships" (line 50-51), but `build_site.py` defines `CLI_PY` but never uses `extract.read_cli()`, and the CLI reference page is just rendered from `docs/cli.md`. Either implement the CLI tree rendering on the site, or fix the README claim.

10. **Fix the README's `infra/cloudflare/` path inaccuracy** — The README Code Overview table (line 73) and `docs/architecture/README.md` (line 16) list `infra/cloudflare/` as containing the Wrangler config, but `wrangler.jsonc` is actually at the repository root.

11. **Add security headers to the Cloudflare Worker** — The `worker.ts` in `infra/cloudflare/` doesn't set any security headers (CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, etc.). For a hosted SaaS product, adding security headers would improve security posture.

12. **Fix the `landing.json` hardcoded "Thirty tools" text** — Lines 180 and 239 hardcode "Thirty tools" as prose text. While the `_works_today` function dynamically generates the count for the status list, the landing page title and the "how" section body have hardcoded counts that would drift if tools are added/removed. These should be dynamically generated.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider. The landing.json "Thirty tools" is in the content JSON, which is static. The `_works_today` function generates the status list dynamically. But the "Thirty tools. One contract." title and the "Thirty tools, at decision time" body are static strings in landing.json. These could drift. But landing.json is not code — it's content. The build_site.py could generate these dynamically, but currently doesn't.

Hmm, but actually this is a real concern. If someone adds a 31st tool, the site would still say "Thirty tools." The test `test_the_tool_count_on_the_page_matches_the_contract` checks `f"See all {len(tools)} tools"` (which is dynamic from the template), but doesn't check the "Thirty tools" text. So this is a real drift risk.

But is this a high-value opportunity? The risk is real but the impact is small (a number on a landing page). Let me think of better alternatives.

13. **Add `--check` mode consistency to the install scripts** — The `scripts/install.sh` and `scripts/install.ps1` don't have a `--check` or `--version` flag. The `scripts/build_binary.sh` has `--check` for build info. But the install scripts could benefit from a `--version` or `--dry-run` option. Actually, this is already in the design — the install scripts just download and install. This might not be a high-value opportunity.

14. **Website: Add `loading="lazy"` to images and add `width`/`height` attributes** — The landing page has images (mark.svg) without dimension attributes, which could cause layout shift. But actually, looking at the templates, images have `width` and `height` attributes already (e.g., `width="24" height="24"`). So this is already handled.

15. **Website: The `website/index.html` file is not covered by tests** — This is the same as #2. Let me think of a different opportunity.

16. **CI: The `tauri-build` job uploads artifacts but doesn't attach them to releases** — Looking at ci.yml, the `tauri-build` job (line 289) uploads `tauri-bundles-linux` artifacts, but the `tauri-release.yml` workflow handles attaching desktop bundles to releases. The CI `tauri-build` job builds bundles but doesn't attach them to releases. This is by design (tauri-release.yml handles it for tagged releases). But the CI `tauri-build` job runs on every push/PR, which is slow. Maybe it could be optimized.

Actually, looking at the CI more carefully:
- `tauri-check` (ci.yml:256) runs `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, and `cargo check` — this is for linting/typecheck
- `tauri-build` (ci.yml:289) actually builds the desktop bundles and uploads them as artifacts

The `tauri-build` job runs on every PR, which is expensive (timeout-minutes: 60). This is for CI signal — does the desktop build work? But it's slow. Maybe this could be optimized by only running it on tagged releases or on demand.

Actually, looking more carefully, the `tauri-build` job in CI only builds Linux bundles (ubuntu-latest, deb and AppImage). The macOS and Windows builds are in `tauri-release.yml` which only runs on tag push. So the CI `tauri-build` job is specifically for Linux CI verification. This seems reasonable.

17. **The `docs/cli.md` mentions `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE` in the connectors reference but the README uses `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG`** — This is part of #5 above.

18. **Website: The `sitemap.xml` doesn't include the `og.png` or other assets** — Looking at build_site.py, the sitemap is generated from the rendered pages. It doesn't include static assets. This is fine for SEO (Google can discover assets from HTML).

19. **The `release_instructions.py` has a bug in the "Verify" section** — Looking at lines 100-107:
```python
lines.append("### Verify")
lines.append("Download ``checksums.txt`` from this release and verify the archive you picked:")
lines.append("")
lines.append("```bash")
lines.append("curl -fsSL -O checksums.txt")

lines.append("sha256sum -c checksums.txt   # or: shasum -a 256 -c checksums.txt")
lines.append("```")
```

Wait, this generates:
```bash

https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/download/v0.12.0/checksums.txt
sha256sum -c checksums.txt   # or: shasum -a 256 -c checksums.txt
```

The `curl -fsSL -O checksums.txt` downloads from the current URL, but then `https://...` is on the next line as if it's a separate command. This seems like a formatting issue — the URL should be part of the curl command. Let me re-read... Actually, looking at line 105: `f"{dl_base}/checksums.txt"` — this just outputs the URL as a separate line, not `curl -fsSL -O {dl_base}/checksums.txt`. This looks like a bug! The verify command should be:
```bash
curl -fsSL -O {dl_base}/checksums.txt
sha256sum -c checksums.txt
```

But instead it outputs:
```bash
curl -fsSL -O checksums.txt
https://github.com/.../checksums.txt
sha256sum -c checksums.txt
```

The second line is just a bare URL, which is not a valid command. This is a bug in the release instructions generator.

Wait, actually, looking at the install.sh's `sha256_verify` function, it downloads the checksums.txt and verifies just the one archive. The release_instructions.py "Verify" section is meant to be user-facing guidance. The bug is that `curl -fsSL -O checksums.txt` would download a file named "checksums.txt" from whatever URL the browser is at, not from the release. And then the next line is just the URL printed as text. This is confusing — it should be `curl -fsSL -O {dl_base}/checksums.txt`.

Actually wait, let me re-read the code more carefully:

```python
lines.append("curl -fsSL -O checksums.txt")
lines.append(f"{dl_base}/checksums.txt")
```

This would produce:
```

https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/download/v0.12.0/checksums.txt

```python

```

This is a real bug! The "Verify" section of the release instructions generates a broken command.

Actually, wait. Let me re-read this. The `curl -fsSL -O` flag downloads a remote file and saves it with the same name as the remote file. Without specifying a URL, `curl -fsSL -O checksums.txt` would try to download from a URL called "checksums.txt" which doesn't exist. The next line `f"{dl_base}/checksums.txt"` is just a string with the URL, printed on its own line, not as part of a command.

```

```
But the URL is split across two lines. This is a bug. The fix would be:

"""Unit tests for scripts/release_instructions.py.

Pure-function coverage: the section generator and the body application
helper. `main()` is exercised with monkeypatched subprocess so no network
or `gh` binary is required.
"""

import subprocess

from release_instructions import apply_instructions, build_instructions_section, main


def test_build_instructions_section_contains_artifacts_and_installers():
    artifacts = [
        {
            "name": "odi_0.7.0_linux_x86_64.tar.gz",
            "browser_download_url": "https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/download/v0.7.0/odi_0.7.0_linux_x86_64.tar.gz",
            "size": 12345,
        },
        {
            "name": "odi_0.7.0_windows_x86_64.zip",
            "browser_download_url": "https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/download/v0.7.0/odi_0.7.0_windows_x86_64.zip",
            "size": 67890,
        },
        {
            "name": "checksums.txt",
            "browser_download_url": "https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/download/v0.7.0/checksums.txt",
            "size": 100,
        },
        {
            "name": "install.sh",
            "browser_download_url": "https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/download/v0.7.0/install.sh",
            "size": 200,
        },
        {
            "name": "install.ps1",
            "browser_download_url": "https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/download/v0.7.0/install.ps1",
            "size": 210,
        },
    ]
    section = build_instructions_section(
        "v0.7.0", "alehar9320/agentic-odi", artifacts, "abc123  odi_0.7.0_linux_x86_64.tar.gz\n"
    )
    assert "## 📦 Download & Run" in section
    assert "<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_START -->" in section
    assert "<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_END -->" in section
    assert artifacts[0]["browser_download_url"] in section
    assert artifacts[1]["browser_download_url"] in section
    assert "checksums.txt" in section
    assert "install.sh | sh" in section
    assert "install.ps1 | iex" in section
    assert "odi --version" in section


def test_apply_instructions_appends_when_no_markers():
    body = "# Changelog\n\n- fix: something\n"
    section = "<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_START -->\nX\n<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_END -->\n"
    out = apply_instructions(body, section)
    assert body in out
    assert "X" in out
    assert out.count("<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_START -->") == 1
    assert out.count("<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_END -->") == 1


def test_apply_instructions_replaces_existing_section_without_duplicating():
    old_section = "<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_START -->\nold\n<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_END -->\n"
    body = "# Changelog\n\n" + old_section + "\n"
    new_section = "<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_START -->\nnew\n<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_END -->\n"
    out = apply_instructions(body, new_section)
    assert out.count("<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_START -->") == 1
    assert out.count("<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_END -->") == 1
    assert "old" not in out
    assert "new" in out
    assert "# Changelog" in out


def test_apply_instructions_handles_none_body():
    section = "<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_START -->\nX\n<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_END -->\n"
    out = apply_instructions(None, section)
    assert "X" in out


def test_build_instructions_section_without_checksums_degrades_to_links_only():
    artifacts = [
        {
            "name": "odi_0.7.0_linux_x86_64.tar.gz",
            "browser_download_url": "https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/download/v0.7.0/odi_0.7.0_linux_x86_64.tar.gz",
            "size": 1,
        },
    ]
    section = build_instructions_section("v0.7.0", "alehar9320/agentic-odi", artifacts, "")
    assert artifacts[0]["browser_download_url"] in section
    assert "checksums.txt" in section
    assert "odi --version" in section


def _is_release_view(cmd, tag):
    return (
        len(cmd) >= 4
        and cmd[0] == "gh"
        and cmd[1] == "release"
        and cmd[2] == "view"
        and cmd[3] == tag
    )


def _is_release_edit(cmd, tag):
    return (
        len(cmd) >= 4
        and cmd[0] == "gh"
        and cmd[1] == "release"
        and cmd[2] == "edit"
        and cmd[3] == tag
    )


def test_main_publishes_instructions(monkeypatch, capsys):
    calls = []

    def fake_run(cmd, **kwargs):
        calls.append(list(cmd))
        if _is_release_view(cmd, "v0.7.0"):

            class R:
                stdout = '{"body": "# Changelog\\n"}'

            return R()
        if len(cmd) >= 2 and cmd[0] == "gh" and cmd[1] == "api":

            class R:
                stdout = (
                    '{"assets": [{"name": "odi_0.7.0_linux_x86_64.tar.gz", '
                    '"browser_download_url": "https://x/dl/odi_0.7.0_linux_x86_64.tar.gz", '
                    '"size": 1}]}'
                )

            return R()

        class R:
            stdout = ""

        return R()

    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", fake_run)
    rc = main(["--tag", "v0.7.0", "--repo", "alehar9320/agentic-odi", "--dry-run"])
    assert rc == 0
    # dry-run: prints the new body and does NOT call gh release edit
    assert not any(_is_release_edit(c, "v0.7.0") for c in calls)
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "https://x/dl/odi_0.7.0_linux_x86_64.tar.gz" in out
    assert "install.sh | sh" in out
    assert "## 📦 Download & Run" in out

## Objective
- Read-only research to find 12 concrete, high-value dev opportunities across docs accuracy/drift, first-run install experience, hosted Studio/deployment, website discoverability/SEO/accessibility/performance, release/version/update flow, CI signal speed/reliability, generated docs, contributor ergonomics, security headers, and broken/stale links or commands.

## Important Details
- Repository: `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi` — a uv workspace with Python (CLI, MCP server, studio-api, core, connectors) + React/Tauri SPA.
- Focus: each candidate must deliver a distinct user/developer-visible increment implementable by a junior agent in 2–4 hours.

## The 12 Opportunities Found

### 1. Broken "Verify" download command on every release page
**File:** `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/scripts/release_instructions.py:104-105`

The `curl` command that users run to download and verify checksums is split across two lines in a way that produces a malformed command: `curl -fsSL -O checksum.txt` ends on one line, then the URL begins on the next. The assembled output is a broken command printed on the release GitHub page.
**Effort:** ~1–2 hours (fix string + test assertion).

### 2. Incorrect MCP tool name in the schema reference page
**File:** `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/website/templates/_mcp_reference.html:52`

The generated MCP reference says `odi_schema` where every other occurrence correctly uses `get_odi_schema`. Line 52 is wrong; lines 57 is right. This is a rendering/template issue, not a code issue.
**Effort:** ~1 hour (fix template + test).

### 3. Version mismatch: `pyproject.toml` says `0.1.0`, releases are at `0.12.0`
**Files:** `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/pyproject.toml:3`, `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/.release-please-manifest.json:3`, git tags `v0.12.0`

The root `pyproject.toml` version is stuck at `0.1.0` while the release-please manifest and git history are at `0.12.0`. A source install reports `odi --version` as `0.1.0`, which is misleading for a project 12 releases deep. The release-please `simple` config does not bind to `pyproject.toml`, so the version never auto-syncs.
**Effort:** ~2 hours (align version + verify release-please config).

### 4. Stale, unused `website/index.html` from a dead build system
**File:** `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/website/index.html`

`website/index.html` is a leftover from an old GitHub Pages redesign (SDD docs reference a `website/tools/sync-readme.py` script that no longer exists). The current Jinja2-based build outputs to `website/dist/index.html`. The root `website/index.html` is stale, out of sync with `README.md`, and unused by any test or the build system.
**Effort:** ~1 hour (verify no consumers + delete).

### 5. False claim: "CLI tree ... read from the code that ships"
**Files:** `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/README.md:50-51`, `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/website/tools/build_site.py:39`, `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/website/tools/extract.py:347`

README claims the site reads the CLI tree "from the code that ships, so they cannot drift from it." In reality, `extract.read_cli()` is defined but **never called** by `build_site.py`. The CLI documentation on the site (`docs/cli.md` content) is hand-maintained Markdown, not extracted from code. The "cannot drift" claim is false.
**Effort:** ~1–2 hours (implement `read_cli()` wiring **or** correct the README claim + test).

### 9. Two different connector config env vars + locations
**Files:** `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/README.md:138`, `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/docs/connectors.md:4`
**Code:** `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/connectors.py:61,88`, `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/paths.py:15,23`

The CLI uses `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE` with default `~/.agentic-odi/connectors.json` (cwd-relative). The connectors library uses `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG` with default `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json` (xdg). README documents `CONFIG`/`~/.config/...` but connectors docs document `FILE`/`.agentic-odi/`. A user following one set of docs can silently end up with two different config files.
**Effort:** ~2–3 hours (unify env var name + path + update docs + tests).

### 10. README says Wrangler config is in `infra/cloudflare/` but it's at the repo root
**Files:** `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/README.md:73`, `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/docs/architecture/README.md:16`

`wrangler.jsonc` lives at `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/wrangler.jsonc` (repo root). `infra/cloudflare/` only contains `worker.ts`.
**Effort:** ~15 minutes (fix both docs).

### 11. Cloudflare Worker serves responses with zero security headers
**File:** `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/infra/cloudflare/worker.ts`

The Worker sets no CSP, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, or `Permissions-Policy`. As the site moves to a hosted deployment, these headers should be added to the Response for defense-in-depth.
**Effort:** ~1–2 hours (add headers + smoke test).
